title: The skeleton's idle stream and its dead stream are byte-identical, and a gap is never recovered
statement: The walking skeleton's `/events` stream sends `retry: 500` once and then nothing until a change occurs: an idle stream emitted zero bytes over six seconds. It sends no `id:` field, so a reconnecting client has no `Last-Event-ID` to present and the server has no position to resume from; a change made while disconnected was not delivered after reconnection. A client therefore cannot distinguish an idle stream from a dead one, and cannot learn that it missed anything.
notes: ⚠️ THIS REFUTES REQ-0018's SECOND CLAUSE FOR THE SUBSTRATE, by construction rather than by accident. The requirement asks that *a dropped update stream is visibly distinguishable from an idle one*. Byte-identical is the strongest possible form of indistinguishable — no client-side cleverness can recover a difference that was never transmitted. ⚠️ AND THE TWO GAPS COMPOUND. Per the WHATWG specification a client usually reconnects on its own (EVD-0054), which sounds like it makes the missed change harmless — it does not, because reconnection delivers nothing and the page only reloads on a message. So the page is stale, correctly connected, and silent, until some unrelated later change happens to arrive. ⚠️ Spec-side caveat carried explicitly: a FAILED connection is terminal and never retried (EVD-0051), and a non-200 or wrong Content-Type causes exactly that (EVD-0053). That path was not exercised here and is the one where the stream is genuinely gone for good. ⚠️ The server half is measured; browser reconnect behaviour is source-supported only.
